data.narrative:
Project Omega, a seed-stage nuclear energy company founded by Stafford Sheehan, has raised $12M to date. The nuclear energy sector comp universe includes 3 public peers (OKLO, NNE, SMR) and 8 private companies, with established players including Nano Nuclear Energy, Oklo, Valar Atomics, X-Energy, and Fuse Energy at various development stages.

A peer-median approach proved inapplicable due to insufficient same-stage and adjacent-stage comparables within the nuclear energy sector—only 1 seed-stage peer and 1 adjacent-stage peer were identified, falling short of the 3-datapoint minimum required for meaningful triangulation. A stage-progression method was therefore applied, using Project Omega's $12M in total capital raised as a base value proxy. Applying a typical 2.5x step-up multiplier from seed to next stage yields an implied valuation of $30M.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $26M to $34M, with a median of $30M. This range reflects the single applicable method and carries material uncertainty given the narrow peer set and absence of direct comparable transactions in early-stage nuclear. The key risk to this valuation is the scarcity of seed-stage nuclear comparables with disclosed terms; broader-market stage progressions may not fully capture sector-specific capital efficiency or regulatory risk. Further datapoints from upcoming nuclear-sector financings would materially improve confidence in this range.
